info.bio: The Nihilist Spasm Band is a unique experimental collective generally known as "the first noise band." Formed in 1965 in London, Ontario, the Canadian group has since improvised on a number of instruments, including homemade creations such as the violin created by bandmember Art Pratten, the "Pratt-a-various." Bandmembers include Pratten (who also plays "water-pipe"), Bill Exley (spoken word), Murray Favro (guitar), John Clement (guitar and drums), John Boyle (drums and kazoo), and Hugh McIntyre (bass).

podcast.title: Documentary and Hall of Fame
podcast.body: There is a documentary about the group, and they are recognized as part of the London Music Hall of Fame. "There's a documentary on the group and they're part of the London Music Hall of Fame."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Famous Fans and Openers
podcast.body: They have garnered fans among notable bands like Sonic Youth, for whom they opened at least once. They also have fans in Negative Land and, surprisingly, R.E.M. "They have fans in Sonic Youth. In fact, they open for Sonic Youth at least once, as well as negative land, other noise groups, and believe it or not, R-E-M."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Longevity
podcast.body: The Nihilist Spasm Band was formed in London, Ontario, in 1965 and remains active, making them a long-standing fixture in the music scene. "They were formed in London, Ontario in 1965 and are still going."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Touring
podcast.body: The Nihilist Spasm Band has toured internationally, performing in countries such as England, France, Switzerland, Germany, the Czech Republic, and Japan. "If, toward England, France, Switzerland, Germany, the Czech Republic, and Japan"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lineup Changes and Replacements
podcast.body: While some original members have passed away, they have been replaced, allowing the band to continue. "Some of the original members have died but have been replaced."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Member Connections
podcast.body: Vocalist Bill Exley was a school teacher to author Malcolm Gladwell. "Author Malcolm Gladwell was taught in school by vocalist Bill Exley."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance Venues
podcast.body: For years, the band was a regular presence in London, performing at various bars and an art gallery. "The Nihilist Spasm band was a fixture in London for years at a couple of bars and an art gallery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sample Track Mention
podcast.body: A sample of their work is mentioned, associated with "when in London, sleep with the York Hotel." "There's a sample of their work, the Nihilist Spasm Band, and when in London, sleep with the York Hotel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Spasm Band Definition
podcast.body: In the context of outsider music, a "Spasm band" is defined as a group that primarily uses homemade instruments and relies heavily on improvisation, with no need for coordination or being in tune. "In the world of outside of music, a Spasm band is a group that uses mostly homemade instruments."
